title: Merapi Run 2026: A Sunrise Half Marathon Up the Slopes of Kaliurang
seo_title: Merapi Run 2026 Review: Kaliurang Half Marathon Guide
meta_description: Honest review of Merapi Run 2026 in Kaliurang, Yogyakarta: a hilly asphalt course on Merapi's slopes, race-day logistics, and who should sign up.
dek: A road race that borrows the drama of Mount Merapi without the mud — expect six unbroken kilometers of climbing, a fast downhill finish, and a hotel-run event that's grown into one of Yogyakarta's bigger sport-tourism dates.
verdict: Merapi Run suits runners who want scenery and a genuine hill workout without technical trail footing — it's asphalt throughout, but don't be fooled into thinking that makes it easy. The early climbing on the 10K and 21K is relentless, rewarded by a fast downhill finish and cool mountain air. Logistics are handled by an experienced hotel-and-zoo partnership with on-site pack pickup, medical support, and insurance. First-timers to Merapi's lower slopes, road runners chasing a scenic PB attempt on the shorter distances, and Jogja-based community runners will get the most out of it; those craving technical trail terrain should look elsewhere.

sections.heading: The Course: Asphalt, But Don't Underestimate It
paragraphs: Merapi Run 2026 takes place on Sunday, 9 August 2026, based out of Griya Persada Convention Hotel & Resort in Kaliurang, Yogyakarta, with four distances on offer: a 21.1km half marathon, 10K, 5K, and a 3K fun run [1,3]. Despite the volcano-slope setting and marketing imagery, this is explicitly a road event — organizers describe the route as fully paved and recommend road shoes over trail shoes, which is a detail worth internalizing before you pack your bag [1]. The half marathon carries roughly 493m of elevation gain across its 21.1km, and the profile is front-loaded: a first-hand account of the 10K course from a past edition describes close to 6km of near-continuous uphill before any relief arrives [4].

That relief, when it comes, is real. The same participant account describes the final stretch easing into about 2km of downhill running into the finish, with a timing checkpoint at Kaliurang's well-known Telogo Putri spot along the way [4]. One runner summed up the grind in blunt terms after that long uphill slog, and the payoff of the downhill finish felt like a gift after the climb.

sections.heading: Conditions on Race Morning
paragraphs: Flag-off times for 2026 are staggered early to beat the heat and give slower categories more daylight: the 21K goes off at 05:00, 10K at 05:30, 5K at 05:45, and the 3K fun run at 06:00 WIB, with cut-off times of 4, 3, 2, and 1.5 hours respectively [1]. Kaliurang sits on Merapi's lower slopes and is genuinely cooler than downtown Yogyakarta, and past coverage of the event has repeatedly leaned on that cool mountain air and panoramic backdrop as part of the sell [5,6]. Even so, the road surface itself has drawn comment in past editions — official materials for the region's asphalt routes note that they mix genuine climbs and descents typical of the Kaliurang contour, so runners should expect a workout rather than a flat scenic jog [6].

Registration terms make clear that runners take on their own risk around weather, terrain, and course conditions, and that entry fees are non-refundable regardless of circumstance — standard language, but worth reading before you commit your slot [2].

sections.heading: Organisation and Race-Week Logistics
paragraphs: The event is run by Griya Persada Convention Hotel & Resort together with Suraloka Zoo, with Unicones Creativa Indonesia handling event organisation, and registration opens on 6 May 2026 with entry fees spanning roughly Rp200,000 to Rp500,000 depending on category [1,2]. Race pack collection for 2026 runs Friday–Saturday, 7–8 August, from 10:00 to 18:00 WIB, at the same Griya Persada venue that hosts the start and finish, which keeps logistics simple for anyone staying nearby [3]. Runner benefits listed for the 2026 edition include a timed bib, race pack, participant jersey, water stations, medical and physio support, a finisher medal, and a half-marathon finisher jersey, alongside post-race entertainment and a local UMKM vendor expo [3].

For the 2025 edition, organizers also spoke publicly about insurance coverage and adequate medical facilities as a stated priority, and a similar standard of participant protection appears to carry into the current edition's messaging [6]. A drop-bag baggage service is available at the Race Village for the day, and there is a mosque roughly 300m north of the hotel for runners who need it before the early flag-off [1].

sections.heading: Field, Atmosphere, and Growth of the Event
paragraphs: Merapi Run has been staged by Griya Persada since 2019, and the 2025 running marked its fifth edition, with organizers targeting around 2,500 runners across the four distances that year [5]. The half marathon category itself is a relatively recent addition — added in 2025 specifically in response to participant demand for a longer distance, according to race director Ronny Yuliananto of Unicones [6]. That growth trajectory suggests an event that's scaling up rather than treading water, with local cultural performances along the route and community-oriented touches like a family-run category built into recent editions [6].

The tone leans toward sport tourism rather than elite competition — past editions have carried thematic branding tied to Kaliurang's history with the 2010 Merapi eruption, with the event positioning itself as much around scenery, local culture, and remembrance as around racing hard [6]. If you're after PB chasing on a fast, flat course, this isn't it; if you want a well-supported reason to visit Kaliurang and push through a proper hill session with a crowd, it fits the bill.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: Sign up for Merapi Run 2026 if you want a scenic, cooler-air alternative to Yogyakarta's flatter city races and don't mind that the mountain setting comes via asphalt rather than singletrack — road shoes are the right call here, not trail shoes [1]. The 10K and 21K in particular reward runners who can grind through sustained early climbing, since the course profile is genuinely hilly rather than an easy scenic outing [4]. Given the non-refundable entry policy and the runner's-own-risk terms around weather and terrain, it's worth registering with clear eyes about what a mountain-slope road race actually demands [2]. For those seeking a shorter, lower-commitment day out, the 5K and 3K options offer the same views and event infrastructure with far less climbing to contend with [3].

faqs.question: Is Merapi Run 2026 a trail race or a road race?
faqs.answer: It's a road race despite the mountain and forest imagery in its promotion. The route is fully paved, so organizers advise road shoes rather than trail shoes for all four distances on offer [1].

faqs.question: What distances can I run at Merapi Run 2026?
faqs.answer: There are four categories: a 21.1km half marathon, a 10K, a 5K, and a 3K fun run, all starting and finishing at Griya Persada Convention Hotel & Resort in Kaliurang [1,3].

faqs.question: When does registration open and how much does it cost?
faqs.answer: Registration for the 2026 edition opens on 6 May 2026, with entry fees ranging roughly from Rp200,000 to Rp500,000 depending on the category chosen [2].

faqs.question: How hilly is the Merapi Run course?
faqs.answer: Genuinely hilly. A past 10K participant described nearly 6km of continuous uphill before the course eased into about 2km of downhill running toward the finish near Telogo Putri [4].
